ACT 2023

2022 SUPPLEMENTARY APPROPRIATION
ACT 2023
(NO. 4 OF 2023)
PASSED by the National Parliament this 19th day of June 2023.
(This printed impression has been carefully compared by me with the Bill passed by
Parliament and found by me to be a true and correct copy of the Bill)
David Kusilifu
Clerk to National Parliament
ASSENTED to in His Majesty’s name and on His Majesty’s behalf this 4th day of
August 2023.
Sir David Vunagi
Governor-General
Date of Commencement: see section 2.
AN ACT TO APPROPRIATE AN ADDITIONAL SEVENTY FOUR MILLION, SIX
HUNDRED AND SIXTY NINE THOUSAND AND SEVEN HUNDRED AND
SIXTY EIGHT DOLLARS TO THE SERVICE OF THE FINANCIAL YEAR
ENDING 31 DECEMBER 2022.
ENACTED BY THE NATIONAL PARLIAMENT OF SOLOMON ISLANDS.

2022 SUPLEMENTARY APPROPRIATION ACT 2023
Table of provisions
1 Short title 1
2 Commencement 1
3 Authorisation of appropriation 1
SCHEDULE 2

2022 SUPPLEMENTARY APPROPRIATION ACT 2023
1 Short title
This Act may be cited as the 2022 Supplementary Appropriation Act
2023.
2 Commencement
This Act commences on the day it is published in the Gazette.
3 Authorisation of appropriation
(1) The issue of an amount of $74,669,768 from the Consolidated Fund
is authorised to be applied to the service of the financial year ending
31 December 2022.
(2) The amount specified in subsection (1) is taken to be appropriated
as from the date this Act commences for the supply of the heads,
and in the amounts respectively specified for the heads, set out in
the Schedule.
Note to section 3.
Section 7 of the 2022 Appropriation Act 2022 provides that the total amounts
authorised by contingency warrants issued by the Minister under section 58 of the
Public Financial Management Act 2013 for the financial year ending 31 December
2022 must not exceed $20,000,000.
Section 6 of the 2022 Appropriation Act 2022 provides that, for section 60(2) of the
Public Financial Management Act 2013, the total amount authorised by advance
warrants issued by the Minister for the financial year ending 31 December 2022
must not at any one time, after deducting repayments and monies on deposit,
exceed $150,000,000.
